title: Typography and number forms per language, fixed by code
description:
As a copy editor, I want a translated page to use its own language's punctuation and number forms, fixed by code, so mechanical slips never reach a reader and never need a model.

Design: sections 1.4 (typography is normative and mechanical: GB/T 15834-2011, the common copywriting guidelines, zhlint and AutoCorrect agree) and 2.3. Chinese and Spanish typography packs are built together (Ryan 2026-11-13). Each rule has a deterministic fix. Spacing between Chinese and Latin text or digits is a house choice, default one space. Quotation marks, ellipsis, dashes, number grouping and date forms come from CLDR plus the pack. Target-locale conventions of naming and register belong in the pack and the per-language glossary, never in code.

```gherkin
Feature: A translated page uses its own language's punctuation and numbers
  Scenario: Half-width punctuation in Chinese is found and fixed
    Given a Chinese sentence ending with "." and using straight double quotes
    When Humanus checks it with the Chinese typography pack
    Then each mark is reported with its replacement
    And applying the replacements gives "。" and "“ ”"

  Scenario: English number words left in Chinese are reported
    Given the Chinese text "低 68 percent，约 50 million 英里"
    When Humanus checks it
    Then "68 percent" is reported with "68%"
    And "50 million" is reported with "5000 万"

  Scenario: Spanish uses its own marks and number forms
    Given the Spanish text 'Dijo "no" y pagó 1,250.50 dólares'
    When Humanus checks it with the Spanish typography pack
    Then the straight quotes are reported with their Spanish replacements
    And "1,250.50" is reported with "1250,50"

  Scenario: A fix is deterministic and re-checking it finds nothing
    Given a Chinese draft whose typography findings were all applied
    When Humanus checks it again
    Then no typography finding is reported
```
